title: Apohara 2.0: A hardware-agnostic compression stack for KV-cache reuse (v5.0 companion systems paper)
description: v5.0 is the companion systems paper for the Apohara 2.0 release. The narrative arc starts at GATE #0 ABANDON (the original KV-sharing mechanism lost to native vLLM APC by 22% throughput and added 147% TTFT) and ends at a 3.94 GiB RAM ceiling for 10M documents at 768-d/4-bit (AUDIT #23b closed by the per-block codec, AUDIT #27). The headline is the 'WOW 8 GB' matrix on an RTX 2060 SUPER: three A/B/C conditions measured end-to-end, with the 'cabe, no es usable' cell preserved as a measured negative result, not papered over. All measurements trace to committed logs; all claims in the paper match the runtime evidence. v4.2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20412807) is the predecessor; this is a new version, not a new record. The full v6.0 paper is the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.20114594 (v3.0).
manual_step_for_pablo: 1. Open https://zenodo.org/ and log in (ORCID-linked account).
2. Navigate to the existing v4.2 record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20412807).
3. Click 'New version' to deposit a v5.0.
4. Upload the three files listed in 'files_to_upload' above.
5. Paste the contents of this JSON into the metadata form (or use the Zenodo REST API to push the same JSON, see https://developers.zenodo.org/).
6. On publish, Zenodo returns a new DOI (typically 10.5281/zenodo.NNNNNNNN).
7. Paste the new DOI back to the assistant; the commit that flips AUDIT #31c to green will then update pyproject.toml:112 and AUDIT.md with the new DOI.
